questions.question: What is denormalization in SQL databases?
questions.answer: Denormalization intentionally introduces redundancy to improve read performance.

questions.question: What is DNS?
questions.answer: Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.

questions.question: What are common uses of triggers?
questions.answer: Triggers are used for auditing, enforcing business rules, logging changes, and maintaining derived data.

questions.question: What is reference counting?
questions.answer: Reference counting tracks how many references point to an object and frees memory when the count reaches zero.

questions.question: What is an abstract class in Java?
questions.answer: An abstract class is a class that cannot be instantiated and may contain abstract and concrete methods.

questions.question: What is relational algebra?
questions.answer: Relational algebra is a procedural query language that operates on relations and forms the theoretical foundation of SQL.

questions.question: What is Floyd-Warshall algorithm?
questions.answer: Floyd-Warshall is a dynamic programming algorithm used to find shortest paths between all pairs of vertices.

questions.question: What is Multilevel Feedback Queue Scheduling?
questions.answer: Multilevel Feedback Queue Scheduling allows processes to move between queues based on their behavior and execution history.

questions.question: What is deadlock prevention?
questions.answer: Deadlock prevention ensures that at least one of the necessary conditions for deadlock never occurs.

questions.question: What is UDP?
questions.answer: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is a connectionless transport protocol that provides fast but unreliable communication.
